title: Availability probing of archive resources (foundational)
description: Every archive resource, chunk file, index, and registry, is probed on a schedule: fetch a byte range and confirm it parses. Probing tests actual retrievability, not just the presence of a directory entry. Failed probes raise incidents immediately rather than waiting for a user to trip over the gap. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Replica inventory with freshness stamps (foundational)
description: The manager keeps an inventory of every replica: location, which resources it mirrors, and the freshness stamp of its last verified sync. The inventory is checked before any restore so recovery never pulls from a stale or unverified copy. Replicas without recent verification are treated as suspect, not as safeties. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Recovery and Redundancy Manager practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Verified restore from replica (foundational)
description: Restoration copies the resource from the freshest verified replica, then verifies the restored copy by hash against the manifest before marking the incident resolved. The post-restore hash check is non-negotiable: a restore that is not verified is just a hopeful copy. Only verified restores close incidents. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
import hashlib
manifest_hash = hashlib.sha256(b'good-data').hexdigest()
restored = b'good-data'  # copied from replica-east
ok = hashlib.sha256(restored).hexdigest() == manifest_hash
print('restore verified:', ok, '-> incident', 'RESOLVED' if ok else 'STILL OPEN')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Recovery and Redundancy Manager practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Redundancy planning per criticality (foundational)
description: Resources are classified by criticality, and each class gets a required replica count: critical data needs three geographically separated copies, ephemeral caches need one. The planner continuously compares actual versus required redundancy and flags under-replicated resources. Planning by criticality spends replica budget where loss would hurt most. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Recovery drill with measured RTO (foundational)
description: Recovery is rehearsed with drills that restore a sample resource and measure the recovery time against the objective. Drills run against replicas, never production, and their measurements feed the redundancy plan. A plan that has never been drilled is a hope, not a plan. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
import time
t0 = time.perf_counter(); time.sleep(0.01); rto = time.perf_counter() - t0
objective = 60.0
print(f'drill RTO: {rto:.2f}s vs objective {objective}s ->', 'PASS' if rto <= objective else 'FAIL')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Archive Recovery and Redundancy Manager practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
